key_insight: A general-purpose language-model agent links materials data, predictive models and reaction networks to turn plain-language research questions into testable synthesis plans.
engineering_relevance: Integrated screening and synthesis planning could help engineers identify functional materials while considering reaction energetics and practical laboratory conditions.
method: Connect the agent to Alexandria’s crystal calculations and trained materials models.
Use a reaction graph to assess candidate stability and synthesis energetics.
Generate synthesis plans and challenge proposed materials with newly generated structures.
evidence_signal: Using about 15 million density-functional calculations and a 17.4-billion-reaction graph, the agent produced unattended case studies covering solar absorbers, an unreported Ba–Zr–S sulfide and an air-stable alternative; web search alone returned literature-discussed proposals.
watch_item: The abstract reports computational proposals and experimental plans, not laboratory validation of the predicted materials or synthesis routes.
paper_title: Materials research with a general-purpose agent
